missions.title: Describe a completed session
missions.concepts: Guided project - functions, loops and session reports
missions.brief: Build `summary_line(name, count, total, available)`, returning one compact summary of completed work.
requirements: `name` is text; strip surrounding spaces and use Learner if it becomes empty.
`count`, `total` and `available` are non-negative integers. `count` is the number of sessions; total and `available` are minutes. When `count` is zero, `total` is also zero.

Return exactly `NAME | N sessions | Hh Mm | Average: A.AA min | Fits: B`. H and M split total into whole hours and remaining minutes; average is total/count with two decimal places, or 0.00 for zero sessions. Fits is `True` when `total <= available`.
Do not print or read input inside this helper. Keep sessions plural even for one.

lesson.heading: A useful application of familiar tools
lesson.text: This project turns individual calculations into a program you can run and export. Start with its report contract; later you will gather several session durations. Zero sessions is a real case, not a division error to ignore.

lesson.heading: Guard a calculation
lesson.text: An `if/else` can choose a calculation before formatting. Only the selected branch executes. Decide what your contract means when a denominator would be zero.

missions.example:
summary_line("  David  ", 3, 85, 90) -> "David | 3 sessions | 1h 25m | Average: 28.33 min | Fits: True"
summary_line(" ", 0, 0, 0) -> "Learner | 0 sessions | 0h 0m | Average: 0.00 min | Fits: True"

tests.hint: Check the stated contract and boundary cases. Use Run to inspect a smaller example.

hints: Separate quantities from their final display.
Which calculation has no valid denominator when count is zero?
Use the explicit zero-session rule before formatting the average. The total remains in minutes for the fit comparison.

notes: Calculations and formatting share one small contract. Named quantities make the result easy to trace.
The zero case is handled before division. An exact budget fit succeeds.

missions.title: Gather different session lengths
missions.concepts: Guided project - functions, loops and session reports
missions.brief: Build `collect_minutes(count)`, which reads one duration for each session and returns their total minutes.
requirements: `count` is a non-negative integer. Read exactly count lines with `input()` and no prompts. Each line is a valid non-negative whole-number duration in minutes.
Return their sum; print nothing from the helper. When `count` is zero, return zero without reading any input. Session durations can differ.

lesson.heading: Repeat a known operation
lesson.text: The review chapter introduced `for` and `range()`. Here the repeat count is supplied by the caller. `range(count)` represents `count` repetitions, and `range(0)` has none.

lesson.heading: Keep state across repetitions
lesson.text: A running total starts before a loop and changes inside it. Assigning it inside the loop would reset it each time. In this project, this helper deliberately owns console input; the report helper owns formatting. These are different responsibilities, so not every helper should be pure.
lesson.code:
points = 0
for turn in range(3):
    points = points + 2
print(points)

collect_minutes(0) -> return 0 without input

The zero-session case should work without a special input read.
An accumulator outside the loop can collect the converted duration from each repetition.

notes: The helper is an input boundary: its callers choose how many values it reads.
A list is unnecessary when only the total is needed. Later chapters will keep individual durations for richer reports.

missions.title: Build the session summary tool
missions.concepts: Guided project - functions, loops and session reports
missions.brief: Build a console tool that reads a session log and prints its summary.
requirements: Read `name`, `count` and available minutes on separate lines in that order, then exactly count durations (one per line). No prompts. All numeric text is valid non-negative whole numbers.

Use `collect_minutes(count)` to return the sum of the durations and `summary_line(name, count, total, available)` to return the report. Implement both helpers and the outer program; you may reuse your own previous submissions.

Print exactly one line: `NAME | N sessions | Hh Mm | Average: A.AA min | Fits: B`. Trim name, falling back to Learner; split total into hours/remainder minutes; average is zero for zero sessions; Fits includes equality.

`collect_minutes` reads durations but prints nothing. `summary_line` reads no input and prints nothing. The outer program prints the returned report. No setup charge is included: these are completed sessions, not planned estimates.

lesson.heading: Bring the pieces together
lesson.text: Reuse your own helpers from this project, then connect their inputs and returned values. This is a program assembly task, not a new algorithm. Keep the report contract available while you work.

lesson.heading: Take it with you
lesson.text: After passing, Download `.py` gives you a real Python source file. On a machine with Python installed, run it as a console program and enter the values one at a time. It reads `stdin` and prints a summary; it does not yet save a log file. We will guide local environment setup before larger projects.

The two helpers have different jobs: gathering work and describing it.
Capture the collected total and supply it to the report helper. Only the outer program prints the final line.

reference.code:
def summary_line(name, count, total, available):
    clean_name = name.strip()
    if clean_name == "":
        clean_name = "Learner"
    if count == 0:
        average = 0
    else:
        average = total / count
    hours = total // 60
    minutes = total % 60
    fits = total <= available
    return f"{clean_name} | {count} sessions | {hours}h {minutes}m | Average: {average:.2f} min | Fits: {fits}"

def collect_minutes(count):
    total = 0
    for session in range(count):
        total = total + int(input())
    return total

name = input()
count = int(input())
available = int(input())
total = collect_minutes(count)
print(summary_line(name, count, total, available))
notes: The outer program connects input to collection to formatting; each stage has an explicit contract.
This is a usable console utility. File persistence, arbitrary invalid input and an interactive menu are future extensions, not hidden requirements.
